research_source: Research JSON provided for ClimaAgro Peru

gaps.title: Personalized, hyper-local climate alerts via WhatsApp
gaps.pain: Small farmers depend on generic forecasts or informal word-of-mouth, leading to poor decisions and crop losses. No existing service delivers actionable, parcel-specific advice through an accessible, low-tech channel like WhatsApp.
gaps.why_now: WhatsApp penetration in rural Peru exceeds 80%; El Niño intensifies climate volatility; insurers and cooperatives seek tools to reduce loss ratios and improve farmer engagement.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pilot with 500 farmers to measure reduction in crop loss versus control group; message open rates and action compliance data.

gaps.title: Integrated insurance-alert system for proactive risk mitigation
gaps.pain: Agricultural insurers lack direct, real-time communication with farmers to prevent claims. Farmers miss preemptive actions, increasing claim rates and premiums, while insurers face high loss ratios.
gaps.why_now: Insurers like La Positiva and Rímac are exploring insurtech partnerships; rising climate risk makes prevention a clear economic incentive.
gaps.evidence_needed: Loss ratio data from an insurer pilot; correlation between alert-driven actions and reduced claims.

gaps.title: Hyper-local agronomic recommendation engine
gaps.pain: Farmers receive generic weather warnings without specific, crop-tailored actions (e.g., cover beans, harvest potatoes early). This gap leaves even informed farmers uncertain about concrete steps.
gaps.why_now: Advances in satellite data and crop modeling enable parcel-level recommendations; cooperatives want value-added services for members.
gaps.evidence_needed: A/B test comparing standard alert vs actionable recommendation on farmer adoption and crop outcomes.

gaps.title: Scalable B2B distribution channel for smallholder services
gaps.pain: Reaching 2.2 million dispersed small farmers individually is cost-prohibitive. No platform efficiently aggregates cooperative and insurer networks to deliver and monetize digital agricultural services.
gaps.why_now: Cooperatives are digitizing membership management; insurers need efficient portfolio communications; a B2B model can unlock rapid, low-cost adoption.
gaps.evidence_needed: Signed letters of intent from 5+ cooperatives and 1 insurer; cost-per-farmer metrics compared to direct-to-consumer alternatives.

gaps.title: Trusted, scientifically validated alerts vs. informal WhatsApp groups
gaps.pain: Farmers often rely on peer-to-peer WhatsApp groups sharing unverified rumors, causing panic or inaction. Government alerts are perceived as inaccurate or irrelevant, leaving a trust vacuum.
gaps.why_now: Misinformation during climate extremes can worsen losses; a credible, branded alert service can become the definitive source, building long-term trust.
gaps.evidence_needed: Net Promoter Score survey comparing trust in ClimaAgro vs. SENAMHI and informal groups among target farmers.

gaps.title: Affordable climate intelligence for smallholder-centric organizations
gaps.pain: Platforms like aWhere and Tomorrow.io are priced for large enterprises, leaving cooperatives and small agribusinesses without cost-effective, actionable climate analytics tailored to smallholders.
gaps.why_now: Climate adaptation funding is increasing; smallholder-focused organizations need affordable tools to manage risk and access donor or government support.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pricing willingness survey among 20 cooperatives; competitor price benchmarking to define a viable subscription tier.

checkpoint_instruction: Validate the recommended gap by conducting 10 in-depth interviews with cooperative managers and insured farmers within 4 weeks to quantify pain intensity, current coping mechanisms, and willingness to adopt a WhatsApp-based alert system.
